citation: Mok A, Haldar S, Lee JCY, et al. Postprandial changes in cardiometabolic disease risk in young Chinese men following isocaloric high or low protein diets, stratified by either high or low meal frequency - a randomized controlled crossover trial. Nutrition Journal. 2016;15:27.
protocol: Isocaloric mixed-meal days (~2000 kcal over the session), high protein (~40% energy) or low protein (~10% energy), as 2 large meals (08:00, 12:30) or 6 small meals (every 1.5 h from 08:00); Table 2 gives foods and macronutrients. Venous blood at 0, 1, 2.5, 4, 5.5, 7, 8.5 h.
population: 10 healthy Chinese men; age 29 ± 7 y; BMI ~21 kg/m2; Singapore.

reports.where: Table 3: concentration at each time point and 8.5 h iAUC for all 4 diet conditions

note: Gives full-day insulin across repeated meals, with protein content and meal frequency varied in a 2x2 design, all as SD in one table. Readers must line the time points up with the meal schedule (Fig. 1). Meal kinds: mixed meal.
